caption:
Welcome Kevorian Barnes (RB, Texas Christian) to the QSE family!

A decorated and explosive running back, Kevorian’s career has been defined by early excellence, sustained production, and a proven ability to rise on the biggest stages. From conference honors as a freshman to impactful performances at the Power Five level, his body of work reflects both talent and resilience.

Career Accolades
• Conference USA Freshman of the Year (2022)
• Conference USA All-Freshman Team (2022)
• Honorable Mention All-Conference USA (2022)
• Dave Campbell’s Texas Football All-Texas College Second Team (2022)

2025 | Senior Season (TCU)
• 443 rushing yards on 97 carries (4.63 yards per carry)
• 3 rushing touchdowns with 10 receptions for 48 yards
• Two 100-yard rushing performances
• 106 yards and 2 TDs vs. Baylor
• 113 yards on just 11 carries vs. North Carolina, highlighted by a 75-yard touchdown run

Established Production (UTSA)
• Multiple seasons as a featured back and starter
• 700+ rushing yards and 6 touchdowns during the 2023 campaign
• Continued efficiency, versatility, and scoring impact throughout 2024

Kevorian’s game blends burst, vision, and finishing ability, allowing him to create explosive plays while carrying the physical demands of the position. His journey reflects perseverance, adaptability, and a readiness for the next level.

Proud to welcome a proven and accomplished playmaker to Quintessentially Sports.

caption:
“Nothing Ever Lasts Forever”

Thank you, TCU Football. Thank you for giving me a new family and countless memories that will be cherished forever. Thank you for surrounding me with the men that I would grow to call my brothers. For years, all I ever wanted to do with my life was play football for TCU. When I look back 50 years from now, I can do so with pride and say I gave everything I had. I became someone that a much younger Franklin would be so proud to be. I thank God every day for giving me this chance to prove that I was good enough to be with the best. I finally played my last football game after 14 long years, and it’s time to hang up my cleats. If I lived my life 100 times over, I think I would choose this every time. 

Best job I ever had.

From Kansas City to Fort Worth, sophomore forward Micah Robinson has made an immediate impact on the Horned Frogs. Appearing in all 32 games of his debut season, Robinson averaged 5.3 points and 1.8 rebounds per game while leading the team in free-throw percentage at 76.5%. Known for his smooth shot and steady presence, he recorded six double-figure scoring games, including a season-best 13 points and three made threes against Oklahoma State.

Before TCU, Robinson was a consensus four-star recruit and one of the highest-rated signees in program history. After standout seasons at Oak Hill Academy and Greenhill School, he brought his versatile game and leadership to the Big 12 stage. Now majoring in communication studies, Micah’s story is just getting started — and his freshman season has already proven he’s a name to watch in purple and white. 🐸✨

caption: I find myself at a loss for words when trying to express how thankful I am for this club. It has illuminated so many corners of life for me, and I’ve had the incredible privilege of meeting some truly amazing and special people through it. I honestly can’t imagine where I’d be if I had never joined; I would have missed out on so much. Thank you, Mom and Dad, for your endless sacrifices that have made all of this possible. Your support has carried me so far and so has your love. To my teammates, thank you for always believing in me, for your constant support, and for helping shape me into a better version of myself. You are my closest friends, and I hope we can all stay close far into the future—each of you is destined for greatness! And to my coaches, thank you for pushing me beyond my limits and making me into the player I am today. Santiago Restrepo, in particular, thank you for believing in me even when I didn’t believe in myself. After 7 years of going to practices every week, traveling across the country to compete, it’s crazy to think it’s all over, but I couldn’t be more excited for this next chapter in my life.  This is the hardest goodbye i’ve had to make, i love each of you. #10out

caption:
WHY DO WE FOCUS SO MUCH ON BARREL STRIKE? Let’s dive into 6 reasons why I think it’s important!

Focusing on barrel strike—the ability to make consistent, powerful contact with the sweet spot of the bat—offers significant benefits for hitters in baseball. Here’s why:

Improved Exit Velocity
Consistently hitting the ball with the barrel generates higher exit velocities, resulting in harder-hit balls. This translates to more extra-base hits and home runs.

Enhanced Power Output
Maximizing energy transfer from the bat to the ball improves power, making you a more dangerous hitter in any lineup.

Consistency
Developing the skill to find the barrel repeatedly makes hitting more reliable and reduces slumps, as you’re consistently making productive contact.

Better Plate Approach
To focus on the barrel, hitters naturally refine their swing mechanics and strike-zone discipline, leading to smarter at-bats.

Confidence Boost
Seeing consistent results from barreling the ball builds confidence and trust in your abilities, which translates to overall better performance at the plate.

caption: A lot of people come together to make a successful football team, more than most realize. Coaches past and present help create the players we are today. The parents and grandparents sacrificing their time to take us to practice or put together team dinners for us. The community driving out of town just to support us. It takes so much more than just the eleven men on the field. To all of those that put in even the slightest bit of their effort to make our dreams come true, thank you. Without you, we wouldn’t be where we are today. To the coaches, thank you for putting in more hours than any of us could imagine just for us to play this amazing sport. To my fellow seniors, God has a plan for each of you, put your faith in him and live life to the fullest. Lastly, to the underclass men, don’t blink, because before you know it, it’ll be taken away and you’ll wish for just one more snap.
